boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Simmon's Bluff record (June 21, 1862) in Operations Against Charleston [June 1862]. Rhind's other North Edisto operations and the planned railroad raid are context. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Regiments; the live field reads zero. Rhind says the Planter carried 4 officers and 70 men of the Fifty-fifth Pennsylvania with the Crusader in support, and that papers found in the camp showed the force at the point to be the Marion Artillery and two companies of the Sixteenth South Carolina, the regiment being 2 miles back. Parker says he put the companies of Captains McJunkin and Barnett into the rifle pits and that McCullough, who had arrived, was to advance with four companies.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and a Union landing-party count; no Confederate strength figure. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Parker says no more than twenty minutes passed between the alarm and the first shot, asks for a signal system, notes that the steamer's masthead lookout directed her fire, and says he could only conjecture whether any force landed. Rhind learned the Confederate dispositions from papers captured in the camp.
claims.rationale: Contemporary statements of warning and knowledge by the two commanders. No original reconnaissance, order or message chain was inspected to establish contemporary knowledge. Surprise in a summary does not independently establish what each commander knew.

claims.value: Rhind says he advanced slowly without firing to draw the Confederate artillery down to the river; Parker says he kept his guns under cover anticipating a landing, and planned a front-and-flank attack had a landing been made. NPS says the Federals were mounting an amphibious expedition to cut the Charleston & Savannah Railroad and abandoned the raid.
claims.rationale: Stated intentions from the two reports; the railroad aim is NPS's framing and is not stated in the inspected reports.

claims.value: Rhind took the Crusader and Planter up the river and himself landed with Captain Bennett's company to burn the camp. Parker, commanding the post, placed the riflemen and battery; McCullough arrived during the action and was ordered forward with four companies. The frozen commanders are Lieutenant A. C. Rhind (US) and Colonel James McCullough (CS).
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; neither listed commander receives automatic sole credit. The post commander in the Confederate report is Parker, not the listed McCullough.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Rhind says a short engagement drove off the Confederates and their camp was captured and destroyed; Parker says the riflemen retreated when enfiladed, that some men landed from the Planter, he thought, and burned the infantry tents, and that the boats then went off.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

open_questions: Evans's June 23 transmittal (read, not selected), the captured orders and letters printed in Navies volume 13, and any report by McCullough or the Fifty-fifth Pennsylvania remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. A. C. Rhind's two June 23, 1862 reports (Official Records of the Navies I, 13) are interested Union accounts. Edward L. Parker's June 21 report (Official Records I, XIV) is an interested Confederate account. No history covering this action was found (Jones's Siege of Charleston does not mention it); the gap is recorded. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
